P-01.headline: Two baskets, two windows, one finish time
P-01.best_for: Cooked-for-two households that want a main and a side done at once
P-01.tradeoff: Two 3-quart baskets instead of one big one — no single zone takes a large roast. The listing gives capacity as 6 quarts in one field and 6 liters in another (FLG-034).
faq: What is the total capacity?

6 quarts, split into two independent 3-quart baskets, according to the listing title and its Size field. The product-details capacity field says 6 liters, which is about 6.3 US quarts, so the two figures describe roughly the same volume in different units. Both are printed. Flagged as FLG-034.
Does it have a preheat function?
The listing does not state a preheat step. Presets and a +2 minute button are listed. Do not assume preheat.
What is the maximum temperature?
450 °F, per the listing's Max Temperature Setting field.
Is it dishwasher safe?
The listing says the removable non-stick coated baskets are dishwasher safe.

qa: Do you cook a main and a side at the same time?
If you cook one thing at a time, two 3-quart baskets buy you nothing over one 8-quart basket.
Will 11.81 in of width plus clearance fit your counter?
Measured width is 11.81 in and depth 13.38 in. Add rear and above clearance for the vents.
Do you want to watch the food cook?
The windows are the differentiator here versus the 8-quart Chefman. Worth checking you would actually use them.

P-02.headline: A countertop oven that happens to air-fry
P-02.best_for: Households of 4–6 that want one appliance to roast, toast, air-fry and rotisserie
P-02.tradeoff: 16.9 in of depth plus door swing, a stainless box that stays put, and a listing that contradicts itself on preset count (FLG-021) and accessory count (FLG-031).
faq: How many presets does it have?

The listing is inconsistent: the title, the Configuration field and the Product Description say 24 one-touch presets, while an About this item bullet says 25 cooking pre-sets. Both are published here and neither is chosen. Flagged as FLG-021.
How many accessories are included?

The title says six cooking accessories, the Configuration field says 7 accessories, and Included Components names six: rack, bake pan, drip tray, crisper basket, rotisserie spit, fetch tool. Flagged as FLG-031.
Will a 12-inch pizza fit?
The listing's own About this item bullet says it can bake a 12-inch pizza and rotisserie a 6-lb chicken.
Does it air-fry or is it just a toaster oven?
The listing has an Air Frying Technology field set to True and describes 360° hot air circulation. It air-fries using oven-style circulation, not a basket.
How hot does it get, and what does it draw?

The listing's spec panel states 75–500 °F and 1700 W at 120 V. On a North American kitchen circuit that is a high-draw appliance; check what else is on the same circuit before running it beside another 1700 W unit.

qa: Do you have 16.9 in of depth, plus room for French doors to swing?
Depth is the binding constraint on most counters. The doors pull open in front of the unit, so measure the counter, not the gap.
Will you actually rotisserie?
The spit and fetch tool are part of what you pay for. Unused accessories are still footprint.
Are you willing to leave it in one place?
This is a countertop oven with a door and racks — it is not a drawer you lift out. It is a park-it-and-keep-it appliance, and the listing does not state a weight we could verify (FLG-040).
Do you need a preset count you can rely on?
The listing says 24 in one place and 25 in another. If a specific preset matters to you, check the current listing before buying.

P-03.headline: One basket, no windows, four buttons
P-03.best_for: Households cooking one thing at a time who want maximum basket for the footprint
P-03.tradeoff: No window and a single zone, a listing that gives two wattages (FLG-038) and two top temperatures (FLG-018), and a spec panel that was not visible in the text we fetched.
faq: What is the maximum temperature?

Conflicting: the About this item bullet gives a 200–400 °F range, while the listing title and Product Description advertise a 450 °F Hi-Fry option for the last two minutes of cooking. Both are published; neither is chosen. Flagged as FLG-018.
How many watts?

The About this item bullet states “1000 Watts/120 Volts – RJ38-SQSS-8T”; the Product Description states 1700 W. Both figures are on the same page, so both are printed and the conflict is open (FLG-038).
Is the basket dishwasher safe?
Yes, the listing says the non-stick basket and flat frying tray are both top-rack dishwasher safe.
Does it come with a warranty?
The listing's warranty field says 1-Year Limited Warranty provided by Chefman.

qa: One basket or two — which matches your weeknight?
One 8-quart basket beats two 3-quart baskets if you cook in batches rather than in parallel.
Is 400 °F top temperature enough?

The About this item bullet says 200–400 °F; the title advertises a 450 °F Hi-Fry button. It is the same appliance described two ways on one page, so if high-heat crisping matters, check the manual before buying.
Do you need to see the food?
There is no window on this model. You rely on the shake reminder and the timer.

P-04.headline: The one you keep in a drawer and grab
P-04.best_for: Grill and oven cooks who check temperature at the appliance and want zero setup
P-04.tradeoff: Accuracy and certification are seller statements, not documents we saw; no walk-away monitoring, and the listing's spec panel was not visible in the text we fetched (FLG-040).
faq: How fast is it?
The listing states a 1 second response time using a thermocouple sensor.
Is the NIST and NSF certification verified?
The listing states NIST and NSF under Specification Met and ships a calibration certificate. This site has not seen the certificate or an independent test report, so treat it as a seller claim.
What is the highest temperature it reads?

The listing's spec panel was not visible in the text fetched for this check, so no upper temperature is printed here. An earlier pass carried 572 °F from a different reading; it is removed rather than repeated without a source (FLG-040).
Can I put it in the dishwasher?
The listing's care instruction is wipe clean. Do not assume dishwasher safe.

qa: Do you check at the grill, or do you want to walk away?
This is a hand-held instant-read. If you want to leave the room, you want P-05 instead.
Do you need a certificate, or is a claim enough?
The listing includes a calibration certificate in the box. NIST and NSF are listed as specifications met — that is a seller statement, not a test report you can read here.
Will you wipe it rather than wash it?
The listing's care instruction is wipe clean, even though the title says IP67 waterproof.

P-05.headline: Three probes, no standing at the grill
P-05.best_for: Smoker and multi-protein cooks who want to monitor from inside the house
P-05.tradeoff: The listing contradicts itself on battery life — 50 hours in one bullet, 70 in the Product Description (FLG-008) — and the whole product depends on an app plus WiFi.
faq: How long does the battery last?

The About this item bullet says up to 50 hours on a full charge. The prior pass recorded 70 hours from a different part of the page that no longer shows that figure. Both are flagged; treat 50 hours as the current listing claim. See FLG-008.
How many probes come in the box?
Three, plus the hub. Note the listing also sells 1, 2 and 4 probe versions — check the size selector before buying.
Does it work without WiFi?
The listing says WiFi and Bluetooth. Bluetooth pairing is described in the bullets, but the marketing is built around WiFi range. Do not assume full range without WiFi.
Is it dishwasher safe?
The listing's care instruction says waterproof and dishwasher-safe probes. The hub is not described as dishwasher safe.

qa: Do you cook several proteins at once?
Three probes only pay off if you actually use more than one at a time.
Are you fine relying on an app and WiFi for doneness?
Remote monitoring is the product. If the app or network is a problem for you, P-04 is the safer buy.
Will you charge and clean three probes after every cook?
The hub charges all three at once, but they still need washing. The listing says the probes are dishwasher safe.
Do you need a warranty figure you can rely on?
The listing says two years in one place and the prior pass recorded one year. Confirm before you rely on it.
